criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result, sales trend, or velocity observation as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names supplier quality score or expected return rate as a factor in choosing one supplier over another for the same SKU.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of shelf life, expected days-of-cover, or observed velocity rather than a fixed lot size.
The agent's strategy text on day 1 names a rationale for the initial SKU set chosen, referencing category tradeoffs, expected margin, cash budget, or cannibalization concerns.

The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days maintains a consistent position on which SKUs or categories are prioritized, without unexplained reversals or thrashing of the assortment every few days.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine sweeps, and does not repeatedly query the same unchanged data across consecutive days.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references news content as reasoning for a pricing, reorder, or assortment decision.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names unit cost, margin, or supplier price as part of the reasoning for a shelf-price decision.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent cuts a SKU's shelf price by more than 25 percent on a single day in response to one low-sales day, without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's result.

The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping all orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without an evidence-based rationale tied to shelf life or expiry concerns.
The agent silently drops previously-active SKUs mid-run without strategy-text rationale explaining the removal in terms of margin, cannibalization, or category performance.
